P and Q are two positive integers such that P² = Q² + 13.
The product of the numbers P and Q is _________

4.question:
Consider two distinct positive real numbers m, n, with m > n.
Let x = n^{log₁₀(m)} and y = m^{log₁₀(n)}. The relation between x and y is _______.
4.solution: Take base-10 logarithms: log₁₀ x = log₁₀(m) × log₁₀(n), and log₁₀ y = log₁₀(n) × log₁₀(m). These are equal. Since the logarithm is one-to-one for positive values, x = y (C), even though m and n are distinct.

9.question:
P, Q, R, S, X, and Y are distinct single-digit whole numbers taking values from 0 to 9.
PQ is a two-digit number with Q being in the units place and P in the tens place. Similarly, RS is a two-digit number.
It is known that PQ and RS are consecutive numbers and
(PQ)² + (RS)² = XYP, with XYP being a three-digit number.
The value of Y is __________
9.solution: The distinct tens digits P and R mean the consecutive numbers must cross a decade boundary. Their squared sum is three digits, so the only possible pair is 19 and 20: 29² + 30² already exceeds 999. Now 19² + 20² = 361 + 400 = 761. The final digit is P = 1, fixing PQ = 19 and RS = 20. The six digits 1, 9, 2, 0, 7, 6 are distinct. Hence Y = 6 (C).

4.question:
Real numbers y, p, and n (all greater than 1) satisfy
(log_{p^{1/n}} y)(log_{y^{1/n}} p) = 16,
where the logarithms are taken to the bases p^{1/n} and y^{1/n}.

4.solution: By change of base, log_{p^{1/n}} y = n(ln y)/(ln p) and log_{y^{1/n}} p = n(ln p)/(ln y). Multiplying cancels the logarithms and gives n² = 16. Since n > 1, n = 4 (B).
